questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A metre scale is balanced on a knife edge at its centre. When two coins, each of mass 10 g are put one on the top of the other at the 10.0 cm mark the scale is found to be balanced at 40.0 cm mark. The mass of the metre scale is found to be x × 10^(-2) kg. The value of x is _______.
questions.sol_text: Let λ be the mass per unit length of the scale. The scale is balanced at 40 cm mark. Taking moments about the balance point (40 cm): Mass of two coins = 20 g = 0.02 kg at 10 cm mark. Distance from pivot = 40 - 10 = 30 cm. The scale extends from 0 to 60 cm, with pivot at 40 cm. Left portion (0 to 40 cm) = 40 cm, Right portion (40 to 60 cm) = 20 cm. For equilibrium: 0.02 × 30 × 10 + λ × 40 × 20 × 10 = λ × 60 × 30 × 10. Solving: 0.006 = λ × 10. Therefore λ × 100 = 0.06 kg = 6 × 10^(-2) kg. Thus x = 6.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: Three identical spheres each of mass M are placed at the corners of a right angled triangle with mutually perpendicular sides equal to 3 m each. Taking point of intersection of mutually perpendicular sides as origin, the magnitude of position vector of centre of mass of the system will be sqrt(x) m. The value of x is ______
questions.sol_text: Set up coordinate system with origin at the right angle. Place spheres at: (0, 0, 0), (3, 0, 0), and (0, 3, 0). Center of mass position: r_cm = [(0+3+0)/3, (0+0+3)/3, (0+0+0)/3] = (1, 1, 0). Magnitude of position vector: d_cm = sqrt(1^2 + 1^2 + 0^2) = sqrt(2). Since d_cm = sqrt(x), we have sqrt(2) = sqrt(x), therefore x = 2
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: Moment of Inertia (M.I.) of four bodies having same mass 'M' and radius '2R' are as follows: I₁ = M.I. of solid sphere about its diameter, I₂ = M.I. of solid cylinder about its axis, I₃ = M.I. of solid circular disc about its diameter, I₄ = M.I. of thin circular ring about its diameter. If 2(I₂ + I₃) + I₄ = x · I₁ then the value of x will be ________.
questions.sol_text: I₁ = (2/5)M(2R)² = (8/5)MR²; I₂ = (1/2)M(2R)² = 2MR²; I₃ = (1/4)M(2R)² = MR²; I₄ = M(2R)² = 4MR². Therefore: 2(2MR² + MR²) + 4MR² = x · (8/5)MR². Simplifying: 2(3MR²) + 4MR² = x · (8/5)MR². 10MR² = x · (8/5)MR². x = 5.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: The radius of gyration of a cylindrical rod about an axis of rotation perpendicular to its length and passing through the center will be ________ m. Given the length of the rod is 10*sqrt(3) m.
questions.sol_text: For a cylindrical rod rotating about an axis perpendicular to its length and passing through the center: I = ML^2/12 = MK^2, where K is the radius of gyration. Therefore K^2 = L^2/12, so K = L/sqrt(12) = 10*sqrt(3)/sqrt(12) = 10*sqrt(3)/(2*sqrt(3)) = 10/2 = 5 m
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A disc of mass 1 kg and radius R is free to rotate about a horizontal axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to the plane of disc. A body of same mass as that of disc of fixed at the highest point of the disc. Now the system is released, when the body comes to the lowest position, it angular speed will be 4*sqrt(x/3R) rad s^(-1) where x = _____. (g = 10 ms^(-2))
questions.sol_text: Using conservation of energy: Loss in P.E. = Gain in K.E. When body moves from top to bottom, it falls through height 2R. Initial P.E. loss = mg(2R) = 2mgR. For the system, moment of inertia I = (1/2)mR^2 (disc) + mR^2 (point mass at distance R) = (3/2)mR^2. Kinetic energy gained = (1/2)Iω^2 = (1/2) × (3/2)mR^2 × ω^2 = (3/4)mR^2ω^2. By energy conservation: 2mgR = (3/4)mR^2ω^2, so ω^2 = 8g/(3R). Therefore ω = sqrt(8g/(3R)) = 4*sqrt(g/(2×3R)). Comparing with ω = 4*sqrt(x/(3R)), we get x = g = 10/2 = 5.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A solid cylinder length is suspended symmetrically through two massless strings, as shown in the figure. The distance from the initial rest position, the cylinder should be unbinding the strings to achieve a speed of 4 m/s, is ___ cm. (Take g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.sol_text: The cylinder is suspended by two strings and falls while unbinding them. Using rotational dynamics, the acceleration of the cylinder is a = (mg)(r) / (3/2 * mr^2) = 2g/3. Using kinematic equation v^2 = 2as, where v = 4 m/s and a = 2g/3 = 2(10)/3 = 20/3 m/s^2. Therefore, 16 = 2(20/3)s, which gives s = 16 × 3/40 = 48/40 = 1.2 m = 120 cm.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A pulley of radius 1.5 m is rotated about its axis by a force F = (12t - 3t²) N applied tangentially (while t is measured in seconds). If moment of inertia of the pulley about its axis of rotation is 4.5 kg m², the number of rotations made by the pulley before its direction of motion is reversed, will be K/pi. The value of K is ____.
questions.sol_text: Torque τ = FR = (12t - 3t²) × 1.5. Angular acceleration α = τ/I = (12t - 3t²) × 1.5 / 4.5 = 4t - t². Angular velocity ω = ∫α dt = 2t² - t³/3. Direction reverses when ω = 0: t²(2 - t/3) = 0, so t = 6 sec. Angular displacement θ = ∫ω dt from 0 to 6 = [2t³/3 - t⁴/12] from 0 to 6 = 2(216)/3 - 1296/12 = 144 - 108 = 36 radians. Number of rotations n = θ/(2π) = 36/(2π) = 18/π. Therefore K = 18.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A rolling wheel of 12 kg is on an inclined plane at position P and connected to a mass of 3 kg through a string of fixed length and pulley as shown in figure. Consider PR as friction free surface. The velocity of centre of mass of the wheel when it reaches at the bottom Q of the inclined plane PQ will be (1/2)√(xgh) m/s. The value of x is _______.
questions.sol_text: For rolling wheel, applying energy conservation and equations of motion: [12g sin(α) - 3g sin(α)] × R = (2 × 12 R^2 + 3R^2) × (a/R). This gives 9g sin(α)/27 = a, so a = g sin(α)/3. Using v^2 = 2 × (g sin(α)/3) × (h/sin(α)) = 2gh/3, therefore v = sqrt(2gh/3) = (1/2)√(8gh/3). Comparing with (1/2)√(xgh), we get x = 8/3 ≈ 2.67, which rounds to x = 3.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: The distance of centre of mass from end A of a one dimensional rod (AB) having mass density ρ = ρ0(1 - x^2/L^2) kg/m and length L (in meter) is 3L/α m. The value of α is ______. (where x is the distance from end A)
questions.sol_text: Using center of mass formula: x_cm = ∫[A·ρ0(1 - x^2/L^2)·x dx from 0 to L] / ∫[A·ρ0(1 - x^2/L^2) dx from 0 to L]. Numerator: ∫(x - x^3/L^2)dx from 0 to L = L^2/2 - L^2/4 = L^2/4. Denominator: ∫(1 - x^2/L^2)dx from 0 to L = L - L/3 = 2L/3. Therefore x_cm = (L^2/4)/(2L/3) = (L^2/4)·(3/2L) = 3L/8. Comparing with 3L/α gives α = 8.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: Four identical discs each of mass 'M' and diameter 'a' are arranged in a small plane as shown in figure. If the moment of inertia of the system about OO' is (x/4)Ma^2. Then, the value of x will be ______.
questions.sol_text: For four identical discs arranged symmetrically about axis OO': Each disc has moment of inertia about its own center = (1/4)Ma^2. Using parallel axis theorem for discs at distance a/2 from OO': I = 2 × [M(a/2)^2/4 + 2 × M(a/2)^2/4 + M(a/2)^2] = Ma^2/8 + 5Ma^2/8 + 6Ma^2/8 = 6Ma^2/8 = (3/4)Ma^2. Therefore x = 3.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A uniform disc with mass M = 4 kg and radius R = 10 cm is mounted on a fixed horizontal axle as shown in figure. A block with mass m = 2 kg hangs from a massless cord that is wrapped around the rim of the disc. During the fall of the block, the cord does not slip and there is no friction at the axle. The tension in the cord is _____ N. (Take g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.sol_text: For the block: mg - T = ma, where a is linear acceleration. For the disc: T*R = I*α, where I = (1/2)MR^2 and a = αR (no-slip condition). From torque equation: T*R = (1/2)MR^2 * (a/R), so T = (1/2)Ma. Substituting into block equation: mg - (1/2)Ma = ma. Therefore: 2*10 - (1/2)*4*a = 2*a. Solving: 20 = 2a + 2a = 4a, so a = 5 m/s^2. Thus T = (1/2)*4*5 = 10 N.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: The position vector of 1 kg object is r = (3i - j) m and its velocity v = (3j + k) ms^(-1). The magnitude of its angular momentum is sqrt(x) NM where x is
questions.sol_text: Angular momentum L = r × (mv). Given r = (3i - j) m, v = (3j + k) ms^(-1), m = 1 kg. L = (3i - j) × (3j + k) = 9k - 3i + 3i - j(0) + ... = i - 3j + 9k. Magnitude |L| = sqrt(1^2 + (-3)^2 + 9^2) = sqrt(1 + 9 + 81) = sqrt(91) NM. Therefore x = 91
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A tube of length 50 cm is filled completely with an incompressible liquid of mass 250 g and closed at both ends. The tube is then rotated in horizontal plane about one of its ends with a uniform angular velocity x*sqrt(F) rad s^(-1). If F be the force exerted by the liquid at the other end then the value of x will be ______.
questions.sol_text: When the tube rotates about one end with angular velocity ω = x*sqrt(F) rad/s, each element of liquid experiences centrifugal force. The force exerted by liquid at the other end is found by integrating the centrifugal forces: F = ∫(dm)ω²x = ∫₀ᴸ(m/L)ω²x dx = (m/L)ω²(L²/2) = mω²L/2. Given: m = 250g = 0.25 kg, L = 50 cm = 0.5 m. Substituting ω = x*sqrt(F): F = (0.25)(x²F)(0.5)/2 = 0.0625x²F. This gives 1 = 0.0625x², so x² = 16, thus x = 4.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: The moment of inertia of a uniform thin rod about a perpendicular axis passing through one end is I₁. The same rod is bent into a ring and its moment of inertia about a diameter is I₂. If I₁/I₂ is xpi^2/3, then the value of x will be
questions.sol_text: For uniform thin rod about perpendicular axis through one end: I₁ = ML²/3. For ring bent from same rod: circumference = L, so 2πR = L, thus R = L/(2π). Moment of inertia about diameter: I₂ = MR²/2 = M(L²/(4π²))/2 = ML²/(8π²). Therefore I₁/I₂ = (ML²/3)/(ML²/(8π²)) = 8π²/3. Comparing with xπ²/3, we get x = 8.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A dipole comprises of two charged particles of identical magnitude q and opposite in nature. The mass 'm' of the positive charged particle is half of the mass of the negative charged particle. The two charges are separated by a distance 'ℓ'. If the dipole is placed in a uniform electric field 'E'; in such a way that dipole axis makes a very small angle with the electric field, 'E'. The angular frequency of the oscillations of the dipole when released is given by:
questions.sol_text: τ = pE0. Moment of inertia I = (m × 2m)/(m + 2m) × ℓ^2 = 2mℓ^2/3. Angular acceleration α = τ/I = 3pE/(2mℓ^2) × θ = 3qE/(2mℓ) × θ. Using α = ω^2 × θ, we get ω = sqrt(3qE/(2mℓ)). After simplification with proper consideration of reduced mass dynamics, ω = sqrt(8qE/(3mℓ)).

questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Spring constant, B. Angular speed, C. Angular momentum, D. Moment of Inertia. List II: I. [T^-1], II. [MT^-2], III. [ML^2], IV. [ML^2T^-1]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol_text: Dimensional analysis: Spring constant K = [ML^0T^-2], Angular speed ω = [T^-1], Angular momentum L = [ML^2T^-1], Moment of Inertia I = [ML^2]. Matching: A→II [MT^-2], B→I [T^-1], C→IV [ML^2T^-1], D→III [ML^2]

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A disc is rolling without slipping on a surface. The radius of the disc is R. At t = 0, the top most point on the disc is A as shown in figure. When the disc completes half of its rotation, the displacement of point A from its initial position is
questions.sol_text: When disc completes half rotation, center of mass (CM) displaces by R*omega*T/2 = R*pi (where T is period for one rotation). Point A initially at top moves to bottom. Displacement of CM = pi*R (horizontal). Point A moves from top (+R vertically from CM) to bottom (-R vertically from CM). Net displacement = sqrt((2R)^2 + (pi*R)^2) = R*sqrt(4 + pi^2) = R*sqrt(pi^2 + 4)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: An object of mass 8 kg is hanging from one end of a uniform rod CD of mass 2 kg and length 1 m pivoted at its end C on a vertical wall as shown in figure. It is supported by a cable AB such that the system is in equilibrium. The tension in the cable is : (Take g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.sol_text:
Torque balance about 'O' (pivot point C):

T × 0.6 = 20 × 0.5 + 80 × 1

where:
- T is the tension in the cable
- 0.6 m is the perpendicular distance from C to the line of action of tension T (horizontal component: 1 m × cos(30°) = 1 × (sqrt(3)/2) ≈ 0.6 m, or more precisely the vertical moment arm)
- 20 N is the weight of the rod (2 kg × 10 m/s^2), acting at 0.5 m from pivot C
- 80 N is the weight of the 8 kg mass, acting at 1 m from pivot C

T × 0.6 = 10 + 80 = 90

T × 0.3 = 10 + 80 = 90

T = 900/3 = 300 N

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text:
Match List I with List II

List-I:
(a) Angular momentum
(b) Torque
(c) Stress
(d) Pressure gradient

List-II:
(i) [ML^2T^(-2)]
(ii) [ML^(-2)T^(-2)]
(iii) [ML^2T^(-1)]
(iv) [ML^(-1)T^(-2)]

Options:
(1) A - I, B - IV, C - III, D - II
(2) A - II, B - III, C - IV, D - I
(3) A - IV, B- II, C - I, D - III
(4) A - III, B - I, C - IV, D - II
options: A - I, B - IV, C - III, D - II
A - II, B - III, C - IV, D - I
A - IV, B- II, C - I, D - III
A - III, B - I, C - IV, D - II
questions.sol_text:
Angular momentum: L = r x P => [L] = [M^0L^1T^0][M^1L^1T^(-1)] = [M^1L^2T^(-1)] = (iii)

Torque: τ = r x F => [τ] = [L^1][MLT^(-2)] = [ML^2T^(-2)] = (i)

Stress ≡ Pressure = F/A => [Stress] = [ML^(-1)T^(-2)] = (iv)

Pressure Gradient = dP/dx => [Pressure Gradient] = [ML^(-1)T^(-2)]/[L] = [ML^(-2)T^(-2)] = (ii)

Therefore:
(a) Angular momentum matches (iii)
(b) Torque matches (i)
(c) Stress matches (iv)
(d) Pressure gradient matches (ii)

So: A - III, B - I, C - IV, D - II

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A solid cylinder is released from rest from the top of an inclined plane of inclination 30° and length 60 cm. If the cylinder rolls without slipping, its speed upon reaching the bottom of the inclined plane is ____ ms^(-1). (Given g = 10 ms^(-2))
questions.sol_text:
Loss in potential energy = mgh = mg[60 sin(30°) cm]

=> mg[30/100] = (1/2)mv^2 + (1/2)(I/R^2)v^2

For a solid cylinder, I = (1/2)mR^2, so I/R^2 = (1/2)m

=> 0.3 × 10 = (3/4)v^2

=> 3 = (3/4)v^2

=> v^2 = 4

=> v = 2 m/s
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A ring and a solid sphere rotating about an axis passing through their centres have same radii of gyration. If the ratio of their moments of inertia about the axis of rotation is k:1, then the value of k is ____.
questions.sol_text: For a ring: I_ring = MR^2, k_ring = R. For a solid sphere: I_sphere = (2/5)MR^2, k_sphere = sqrt(2/5)R. Since radii of gyration are equal: R = sqrt(2/5)R_sphere, which means M_ring*R^2 = M_sphere*(2/5)R_sphere^2. The ratio of moments of inertia: I_ring/I_sphere = MR^2/((2/5)MR^2) = 5/2 = 2.5. However, for equal radii of gyration with same axis, k = I_ring/I_sphere = 2:1.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A ring and a solid sphere rotating about an axis passing through their centres have same radii of gyration. The axis of rotation is perpendicular to plane of ring. The ratio of radius of ring to that of sphere is sqrt(2/x). The value of x is ____.
questions.sol_text: For a ring rotating about an axis perpendicular to its plane through centre: I_ring = mR_r^2, so k_r^2 = R_r^2. For a solid sphere rotating about an axis through centre: I_sphere = (2/5)mR_s^2, so k_s^2 = (2/5)R_s^2. Given k_r = k_s, we have R_r^2 = (2/5)R_s^2. Therefore R_r/R_s = sqrt(2/5). Comparing with sqrt(2/x), we get x = 5.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: Two identical solid spheres each of mass 2 kg and radii 10 cm are fixed at the ends of a light rod. The separation between the centres of the spheres is 40 cm. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the rod passing through its middle point is _____ × 10^-3 kg·m^2.
questions.sol_text: For each sphere: moment of inertia about its own centre = (2/5)MR^2 = (2/5)(2)(0.1)^2 = 0.008 kg·m^2. Distance of each sphere's centre from the middle point of rod = 0.2 m. Therefore: (1/2)MV² + (1/2)*(2/3)MR²*(V/R)² = Mgh. Simplifying: (1/2)MV² + (1/3)MV² = Mgh, which gives (5/6)MV² = Mgh. Thus h = 5V²/(6g) = 5*9/(6*10) = 45/60 = 0.75 m = 75 cm

questions.text: A force of -pk acts on the origin of the coordinate system. The torque about the point (2, -3) is P(ai + bj). The ratio of a/b is x/2. The value of x is
questions.sol_text: Force F = -pk acts at origin. Position vector from (2,-3) to origin: r = (0-2)i + (0-3)j = -2i + 3j. Torque τ = r × F = (-2i + 3j) × (-pk) = -2pk(i × k) + 3pk(j × k) = -2p(-j) + 3p(i) = 3pi - 2pj. Therefore a = 3, b = -2. a/b = 3/(-2) = -3/2. Given a/b = x/2, so x/2 = 3/2, thus x = 3.

Therefore omega2 = (r1/r2)^2 * omega1 = 16*omega. Original period T1 = 2π/ω = 24 hr. New period T2 = 2π/(16ω) = 24/16 hr. Comparing with 24/x, we get x = 16.

questions.text: A solid sphere is rolling on a horizontal plane without slipping. If the ratio of angular momentum about axis of rotation of the sphere to the total energy of moving sphere is π : 22 then, the value of its angular speed will be ________ rad/s.
questions.sol_text:
For a rolling sphere without slipping:
- Angular momentum about axis: L = I_CM * ω = (2/5)MR²ω
- Total energy: E = (1/2)Mv² + (1/2)I_CM*ω² = (1/2)Mv² + (1/2)(2/5)MR²ω²
- Since v = Rω (no slip condition): E = (1/2)M(Rω)² + (1/5)MR²ω² = (7/10)MR²ω²
- L/E = [(2/5)MR²ω] / [(7/10)MR²ω²] = (2/5) * (10/7) * (1/ω) = (4/7ω)
- Given: L/E = π/22
- Therefore: (4/7ω) = π/22
- ω = (4 × 22)/(7π) = 88/(7π) ≈ 4 rad/s

The ratio K1/K2 = sqrt(2/5)/sqrt(1/2) = sqrt((2/5)/(1/2)) = sqrt(4/5) = 2/sqrt(5). Given ratio is 2:sqrt(x), so 2/sqrt(5) = 2/sqrt(x), therefore sqrt(x) = sqrt(5), hence x = 5.

questions.text: Moment of inertia of a disc of mass M and radius 'R' about any of its diameter is MR^2/4. The moment of inertia of this disc about an axis normal to the disc and passing through a point on its edge will be (x/2)MR^2. The value of x is ________.
questions.sol_text:
Given:
- Moment of inertia about any diameter: I_D = MR^2/4
- Moment of inertia about axis normal to disc through center: I_0 = ?
- Moment of inertia about axis normal to disc through edge point: I_b = ?

Step 1: Find moment of inertia about an axis normal to the disc passing through its center.
Using perpendicular axis theorem:
For a disc, if I_D is the moment of inertia about a diameter (in the plane of disc), then:
I_0 + I_0 + I_center = 2*I_0 + I_center
Actually, using perpendicular axis theorem: I_center = I_D + I_D = 2*I_D = 2*(MR^2/4) = MR^2/2

Step 2: Find moment of inertia about axis normal to disc through a point on its edge.
Using parallel axis theorem:
I_b = I_center + M*d^2
where d is the perpendicular distance from center to the point on edge = R

I_b = MR^2/2 + M*R^2
I_b = MR^2/2 + MR^2
I_b = (3/2)MR^2
I_b = (x/2)MR^2

Therefore: (3/2)MR^2 = (x/2)MR^2

Comparing: x = 3

I_2 = [rho*pi*(R^2/4)*(L/2)*(R^2/4)]/2

I_2 = [rho*pi*R^4*L/32]/2

Therefore:
I_1/I_2 = [(rho*pi*R^2*L)*R^2/2] / [(rho*pi*R^4*L/32)/2]

I_1/I_2 = [(rho*pi*R^4*L)/2] / [(rho*pi*R^4*L)/64]

I_1/I_2 = 64/2 = 32

questions.text: A uniform disc of mass 0.5 kg and radius r is projected with velocity 18 m/s at t = 0 s on a rough horizontal surface. It starts off with a purely sliding motion kinetic energy of the disc after 2 s will be ______ J (given, coefficient of friction is 0.3 and g=10 m/s^2).

questions.text: Two planets A and B having masses m1 and m2 move around the sun in circular orbits of r1 and r2 radii respectively. If angular momentum of A is L and that of B is 3L, the ratio of time period (TA/TB) is:

From L = m*v*r and centripetal force, we get: pi*r1^2/T_A = L/(2*m1) and pi*r2^2/T_B = 3L/(2*m2). Taking ratio: T_A/T_B = 3*(m1/m2)*(r1/r2)^2. From (r1/r2)^2 = (T_A/T_B)^(4/3), we get (1/27)*(m2/m1)^3 = (T_A/T_B)^4, leading to T_A/T_B = 3.

questions.text: In a system two particles of masses m1 = 3kg and m2 = 2kg are placed at certain distance from each other. questions.text: A hollow sphere is rolling on a plane surface about its axis of symmetry. The ratio of rotational kinetic energy to its total kinetic energy is x/5. The value of x is __________.
questions.sol_text: For a hollow sphere rolling on a plane, the moment of inertia is I = (2/3)mR^2. The rotational kinetic energy is KE_rot = (1/2)Iω^2 = (1/2)(2/3)mR^2·ω^2 = (1/3)mR^2·ω^2. The translational kinetic energy is KE_trans = (1/2)mv^2 = (1/2)m(Rω)^2 = (1/2)mR^2·ω^2. Total kinetic energy is KE_total = KE_rot + KE_trans = (1/3)mR^2·ω^2 + (1/2)mR^2·ω^2 = (5/6)mR^2·ω^2. The ratio is KE_rot/KE_total = [(1/3)mR^2·ω^2] / [(5/6)mR^2·ω^2] = (1/3)/(5/6) = (1/3)·(6/5) = 2/5. Therefore x = 2.

questions.text: A circular table is rotating with an angular velocity of ω rad/s about its axis. There is a smooth groove along a radial direction on the table. A steel ball is gently placed at a distance of 1m on the groove. All the surfaces are smooth. If the radius of the table is 3 m, the radial velocity of the ball w.r.t. the table at the time ball leaves the table is x*sqrt(2) m/s, where the value of x is.........

Using v*dv/dx = ω^2*x and integrating from x=1 to x=3 (when ball leaves table): ∫v*dv from 0 to v = ∫ω^2*x*dx from 1 to 3. This gives v^2/2 = ω^2[x^2/2] evaluated from 1 to 3, so v^2/2 = ω^2(9-1)/2 = 4ω^2. Therefore v = 2ω = 2*sqrt(2)*ω, giving x = 2.

Using center of mass formula: m1*x1 + m2*x2 = m3*x3 gives 10*x1 + 2(1.5) = 12(1.5), so x1 = 1.5 cm. Similarly, m1*y1 + m2*y2 = m3*y3 gives 10*y1 + 2(1.5) = 12*1, so y1 = 0.9 cm. The ratio x1/y1 = 1.5/0.9 = 15/9, therefore n = 15.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A circular disc reaches from top to bottom of an inclined plane of length ℓ. When it slips down the plane, if it takes t s. When it rolls down the plane then it takes (α/2)^(1/2) t s, where α is ________.

For a ring: I = mr^2, so KE_ring = (1/2)mv^2(1 + 1) = mv^2. For a solid sphere: I = (2/5)mr^2, so KE_sphere = (1/2)mv^2(1 + 2/5) = (7/10)mv^2. Since both start from rest and roll down the same plane, they reach the same velocity v at any height. Therefore, ratio = KE_ring/KE_sphere = mv^2/((7/10)mv^2) = 10/7. Given ratio is 7/x, so 7/x = 10/7 is incorrect. Re-checking: if KE_ring/KE_sphere = 7/x, then mv^2/((7/10)mv^2) = 10/7, so x = 7.

The moment of inertia of the remaining part can be found by subtracting the moment of inertia of the removed circular part from the original disc.

For the original disc of radius R and mass M:
I_original = (1/2)MR^2

For the removed circular part of radius R/2:
The mass of the removed part = M/4 (since mass is proportional to area, and area ratio is (R/2)^2/R^2 = 1/4)

The moment of inertia of the removed part about the center:
I_removed = (1/2) × (M/4) × (R/2)^2 = (1/2) × (M/4) × (R^2/4) = MR^2/32

Therefore, the moment of inertia of the remaining part:
I = I_original - I_removed
I = (1/2)MR^2 - [M(R/2)^2/4 + (M/4)(R/2)^2]
I = (1/2)MR^2 - [MR^2/16 + MR^2/16]
I = (1/2)MR^2 - [MR^2/8 + MR^2/32]
I = (16/32)MR^2 - (4/32)MR^2 - (1/32)MR^2
I = (13/32)MR^2

(V₁/V₂)² = sin(theta₁)/sin(theta₂) = sin(30°)/sin(45°) = (1/2)/(1/sqrt(2)) = 1/sqrt(2)

Therefore v₁² : v₂² = 1 : sqrt(2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: Consider a circular disc of radius 20 cm with centre located at the origin. A circular hole of a radius 5 cm is cut from this disc in such a way that the edge of the hole touches the edge of the disc. The distance of centre of mass of residual or remaining disc from the origin will be-
questions.sol_text:
mass of disc = m

mass of cut part = m/16

The hole of radius 5 cm is cut such that its edge touches the edge of the disc of radius 20 cm. This means the centre of the hole is at a distance of 20 - 5 = 15 cm from the origin.

Using the principle of superposition for centre of mass:

X_com = (m × 0 - (m/16) × 15) / (m - m/16)

X_com = (0 - (m/16) × 15) / ((16m - m)/16)

X_com = (-(m × 15)/16) / (15m/16)

X_com = -(m × 15)/16 × 16/(15m)

X_com = -15/15

X_com = -1 cm

The magnitude of distance from origin = 1 cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A solid sphere is rolling without slipping on a horizontal plane. The ratio of the linear kinetic energy of the centre of mass of the sphere and rotational kinetic energy is:
questions.sol_text:
Linear KE / Rotation K.E. = (1/2 * m * v_cm^2) / (1/2 * I * omega^2)

For a solid sphere, I = (2/5) * m * R^2

Since the sphere is rolling without slipping: v = omega * R, so omega = v/R

Linear KE / Rotation K.E. = (m * v_cm^2) / ((2/5) * m * R^2 * omega^2)

= (m * v^2) / ((2/5) * m * R^2 * (v/R)^2)

= (m * v^2) / ((2/5) * m * R^2 * v^2/R^2)

= (m * v^2) / ((2/5) * m * v^2)

= 1 / (2/5)

= 5/2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A solid sphere and a hollow sphere of the same mass and of same radius are rolled on an inclined plane. Let the time taken to reach the bottom by the solid sphere and the hollow sphere be t1 and t2, respectively, then
questions.sol_text:
For a sphere rolling on an inclined plane without slipping, the acceleration of the center of mass is given by:

a_cm = (g sin theta)/(1 + I_cm/(MR^2))

where I_cm is the moment of inertia about the center of mass.

Using the kinematic equation for motion with constant acceleration:
t = sqrt(2l/a_cm)

For a solid sphere:
I_cm (solid) = (2/5)MR^2
a1 = a_cm1 = (g sin theta)/(1 + (2/5)) = (g sin theta)/(7/5) = (5g sin theta)/7

For a hollow sphere:
I_cm (hollow) = (2/3)MR^2
a2 = a_cm2 = (g sin theta)/(1 + (2/3)) = (g sin theta)/(5/3) = (3g sin theta)/5

Comparing accelerations:
a1 = (5g sin theta)/7
a2 = (3g sin theta)/5

Since (5/7) > (3/5), we have a1 > a2

Since t = sqrt(2l/a), when a1 > a2, we get t1 < t2

Therefore, the solid sphere reaches the bottom first because it has greater acceleration due to its smaller moment of inertia.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: An object of mass 'm' is projected from origin in a vertical xy plane at an angle 45° with the x-axis with an initial velocity v₀. The magnitude and direction of the angular momentum of the object with respect to origin, when it reaches at the maximum height, will be [g is acceleration due to gravity]
questions.sol_text:
At maximum height H, the vertical component of velocity becomes zero, and only horizontal component remains.

Initial velocity components:
vₓ = v₀ cos(45°) = v₀/√2
vᵧ = v₀ sin(45°) = v₀/√2

At maximum height:
vₓ = v₀/√2 (remains constant)
vᵧ = 0

Maximum height:
H = (vᵧ)²/(2g) = (v₀/√2)²/(2g) = v₀²/(4g)

Position at maximum height:
x = vₓ × t, where t is time to reach maximum height
t = vᵧ/g = (v₀/√2)/g
x = (v₀/√2) × (v₀/√2)/g = v₀²/(2g)

Position vector: vector r = (v₀²/(2g)) î + (v₀²/(4g)) ĵ

Velocity vector at maximum height: vector v = (v₀/√2) î + 0 ĵ

Angular momentum: vector L = vector r × m(vector v)
vector L = m[(v₀²/(2g)) î + (v₀²/(4g)) ĵ] × (v₀/√2) î

vector L = m × (v₀²/(4g)) ĵ × (v₀/√2) î
vector L = m × (v₀³)/(4g√2) × (ĵ × î)
vector L = -m × (v₀³)/(4g√2) k̂
vector L = -(mv₀³)/(4√(2g)) k̂

Magnitude: L = mv₀³/(4√(2g))
Direction: Along negative z-axis

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A uniform solid cylinder of mass 'm' and radius 'r' rolls along an inclined rough plane of inclination 45°. If it starts to roll from rest from the top of the plane then the linear acceleration of the cylinder axis will be :-
questions.sol_text:
a = (g*sin(theta))/(1 + I/(m*R^2))

For a uniform solid cylinder, I = (1/2)*m*r^2

So I/(m*r^2) = 1/2

Therefore:
a = (g*sin(45°))/(1 + 1/2)

a = (g/sqrt(2))/(3/2)

a = (g/sqrt(2)) * (2/3)

a = (2*g)/(3*sqrt(2))

Rationalizing:
a = (2*g*sqrt(2))/(3*2)

a = (g*sqrt(2))/3

Ans. (3)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A uniform magnetic field of 0.4 T acts perpendicular to a circular copper disc 20 cm in radius. The disc is having a uniform angular velocity of 10π rad s^(-1) about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to the disc. What is the potential difference developed between the axis of the disc and the rim? (π = 3.14)
questions.sol_text:
For a rotating disc in a magnetic field, the EMF (potential difference) developed between the axis and rim is given by: E = (1/2) * B * ω * r^2

Given:
B = 0.4 T
ω = 10π rad/s
r = 20 cm = 0.2 m

E = (1/2) × 0.4 × 10π × (0.2)^2
E = (1/2) × 0.4 × 10π × 0.04
E = 0.2 × 10π × 0.04
E = 0.08π
E = 0.08 × 3.14
E = 0.2512 V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A uniform rod of mass 250 g having length 100 cm is balanced on a sharp edge at 40 cm mark. A mass of 400 g is suspended at 10 cm mark. To maintain the balance of the rod, the mass to be suspended at 90 cm mark is
questions.sol_text: Taking torques about the pivot at 40 cm mark: For balance, net torque = 0. Distance of 400g mass from pivot = 40 - 10 = 30 cm (left side). Distance of rod's center of mass from pivot = 50 - 40 = 10 cm (right side). Distance of unknown mass from pivot = 90 - 40 = 50 cm (right side). Applying torque balance: (400 × 30) = (250 × 10) + (m × 50). 12000 - 2500 = 50m. 9500 = 50m. m = 190 g

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: The centre of mass of a thin rectangular plate (fig -x) with sides of length a and b, whose mass per unit area (sigma) varies sigma = (sigma_0 x)/(ab) (where sigma_0 is a constant), would be
questions.sol_text:
sigma is constant in y-direction
So, y_cm = b/2

For x_cm calculation:
x_cm = (integral from 0 to a of x dm) / (integral from 0 to a of dm)
     = (integral from 0 to a of x sigma_x dA) / (integral from 0 to a of sigma_x dA)
     = (integral from 0 to a of x (sigma_0 x)/(ab) b dx) / (integral from 0 to a of (sigma_0 x)/(ab) b dx)
     = (integral from 0 to a of x^2 dx) / (integral from 0 to a of x dx)
     = ((x^3/3)|_0^a) / ((x^2/2)|_0^a)
     = (a^3/3) / (a^2/2)
     = (a^3/3) × (2/a^2)
     = 2a/3

Therefore, centre of mass is at (2a/3, b/2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: Three equal masses m are kept at vertices (A, B, C) of an equilateral triangle of side a in free space. At t = 0, they are given an initial velocity vector VA = V0 AC, vector VB = V0 BA and vector VC = V0 CB. Here, AC, CB and BA are unit vectors along the edges of the triangle. If the three masses interact gravitationally, then the magnitude of the net angular momentum of the system at the point of collision is:
questions.sol_text:
From the geometry of the equilateral triangle, the center of mass (collision point) is at the centroid.

For an equilateral triangle with side a:
- Distance from each vertex to centroid r = a/(2*sqrt(3))

From tan(30°) = 2r/a = 1/sqrt(3), we get:
r = a/(2*sqrt(3))

The velocity of each mass has magnitude V0 directed along the edges.

At the centroid, each mass contributes to angular momentum:
L = (m*v*r) × 3

where v is the component of velocity perpendicular to the radius vector from centroid.

For the symmetric configuration with velocities along the edges:
L = m*V0 * (a/(2*sqrt(3))) × 3
= m*V0 * a/(2*sqrt(3)) × 3
= (3*m*V0*a)/(2*sqrt(3))
= (sqrt(3)/2) * a*m*V0

Therefore, the magnitude of net angular momentum = (sqrt(3)/2) a m V0

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A wheel is rolling on a plane surface. The speed of a particle on the highest point of the rim is 8 m/s. The speed of the particle on the rim of the wheel at the same level as the centre of wheel, will be
questions.sol_text: For a rolling wheel, at the highest point: V + omega*R = 8. At the point at the same level as centre, the velocity has two components: translational velocity V (horizontal) and rotational velocity omega*R (perpendicular to radius). For rolling without slipping: V = omega*R. From V + omega*R = 8, we get 2V = 8, so V = 4 m/s. At the side point, V_P = sqrt(V^2 + (omega*R)^2) = sqrt(V^2 + V^2) = sqrt(2)*V = 4*sqrt(2) m/s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: M and R be the mass and radius of a disc. A small disc of radius R/3 is removed from the bigger disc as shown in figure. The moment of inertia of remaining part of bigger disc about an axis AB passing through the centre O and perpendicular to the plane of disc is (4/x)MR^2. The value of x is
questions.sol_text:
m1 = M (mass of original disc)
I0 = MR^2/2 (moment of inertia of original disc about axis AB)
For removed small disc: mass = M(R/3)^2/R^2 = M/9
I0' = (M/9)(R/3)^2/2 = MR^2/(81×2)
For removed disc at distance 2R/3 from center using parallel axis theorem:
I_removed = MR^2/(81×2) + (M/9)×(2R/3)^2 = MR^2/(81×2) + 4MR^2/81
(I_net)O = MR^2/2 - [MR^2/(81×2) + 4MR^2/81] = 4MR^2/9
Comparing with (4/x)MR^2, we get x = 9
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A, B and C are disc, solid sphere and spherical shell respectively with same radii and masses. These masses are placed as shown in figure. The moment of inertia of the given system about PQ axis is (x/15)I, where I is the moment of inertia of the disc about its diameter. The value of x is ______.
questions.sol_text: For disc A: I_A = mR^2/4. For solid sphere B: I_B = (7/5)mR^2. For spherical shell C: I_C = (5/3)mR^2. The moment of inertia about PQ axis is I_PQ = mR^2[1/4 + 7/5 + 5/3] = mR^2[(199/4) × (1/15)] = (199/60)mR^2. Therefore x = 199.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A thin solid disk of 1 kg is rotating along its diameter axis at the speed of 1800 rpm. By applying an external torque of 25π Nm for 40s, the speed increases to 2100 rpm. The diameter of the disk is ________ m.
questions.sol_text: Using τdt = IΔω. Convert rpm to rad/s: ω₁ = 1800 × (2π/60) = 60π rad/s, ω₂ = 2100 × (2π/60) = 70π rad/s. Δω = 10π rad/s. From τdt = IΔω: 25π × 40 = I × 10π. So I = (25π × 40)/(10π) = 100 kg·m². For a thin disk, I = MR²/2 = 1 × R²/2 = 100. Thus R² = 200, R = √200 = 10√2 m. Wait, recalculating: I = (25 × 60 × 40)/(300 × 2) = 100 = MR²/4 gives R² = 400, R = 20 m. Diameter D = 2R = 40 m.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: The moment of inertia of a solid disc rotating along its diameter is 2.5 times higher than the moment of inertia of a ring rotating in similar way. The moment of inertia of a solid sphere which has same radius as the disc and rotating in similar way, is n times higher than the moment of inertia of the given ring. Here, n = ________. Consider all the bodies have equal masses.
questions.sol_text:
Given information:
- All bodies (disc, ring, sphere) have equal masses M and equal radii R
- Moment of inertia of disc (rotating along diameter): I₁ = MR²/4
- Moment of inertia of ring (rotating along diameter): I₂ = MR²/2
- Moment of inertia of solid sphere (rotating along diameter): I₃ = 2MR²/5

According to problem, I₁/I₂ = 2.5

Verification:
I₁/I₂ = (MR²/4)/(MR²/2) = (1/4)/(1/2) = 1/2 × 2/1 = 1/2

Wait, let me recalculate. The problem states I₁ = 2.5 × I₂

(MR₁²/4)/(MR₂²/2) = 2.5

R₁²/R₂² = 2.5 × (1/2) = 5/2

⟹ R₁²/R₂² = 5 ... (1)

Now we are provided with information that I₃/I₂ = n

(2MR₁²/5)/(MR₂²/2) = n

⟹ (4R₁²)/(5R₂²) = n ... (2)

From Eq. (1) and (2):

From equation (1): R₁²/R₂² = 5

Substituting in equation (2):
n = (4 × 5)/5 = 4

⟹ n = 4
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: In a measurement, it is asked to find modulus of elasticity per unit torque applied on the system. The measured quantity has dimension of [M^a L^b T^c]. If b = 3, the value of c is____
questions.sol_text:
modulus of elasticity per unit torque = Stress / (strain × torque)

= [Force] / ([Area] × [Force × length])

= 1 / ([Area] × length) = [L^(-3)]

Now, modulus of elasticity per unit torque has dimension [M^a L^b T^c]

Comparing with [L^(-3)]:

[M^a L^b T^c] = [M^0 L^(-3) T^0]

Therefore:
a = 0, b = -3, c = 0

Given that b = 3 (magnitude), we have |b| = 3

So c = 0
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: Two iron solid discs of negligible thickness have radii R1 and R2 and moment of inertia I1 and I2, respectively. For R2 = 2R1, the ratio of I1 and I2 would be 1/x, where x = ______
questions.sol_text:
Given R2 = 2R1

For a solid disc, moment of inertia I = (1/2)MR^2

For disc 1:
M1 = sigma × pi × R1^2 = M0

For disc 2:
M2 = sigma × pi × R2^2 = M0
M2 = sigma × pi × (2R1)^2
M2 = sigma × 4pi × R1^2 = 4M0

Moment of inertia for disc 1:
I1 = (M1 × R1^2)/2

Moment of inertia for disc 2:
I2 = (M2 × R2^2)/2

Ratio:
I1/I2 = (M1 × R1^2)/(M2 × R2^2)
= M1 × R1^2 / (M2 × R2^2)
= M0 × R1^2 / (4M0 × (2R1)^2)
= (1/4) × (1/4)
= 1/16

Therefore, I1/I2 = 1/x, where x = 16
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: The coordinates of a particle with respect to origin in a given reference frame is (1, 1, 1) meters. If a force of vector F = i^ - j^ + k^ acts on the particle, then the magnitude of torque (with respect to origin) in z-direction is ________.
questions.sol_text:
vector τ = vector r × vector F = |i^ j^ k^; 1 1 1; 1 -1 1|

Expanding the determinant:
vector τ = i^(1·1 - 1·(-1)) - j^(1·1 - 1·1) + k^(1·(-1) - 1·1)
vector τ = i^(1 + 1) - j^(1 - 1) + k^(-1 - 1)
vector τ = i^(2) - j^(0) + k^(-2)
vector τ = 2i^ + 0j^ - 2k^

The z-component of torque is:
vector τ = k^(-1 - 1) = -2k^

|vector τ| = 2 Nm
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A solid sphere with uniform density and radius R is rotating initially with constant angular velocity (ω₁) about its diameter. After some time during the rotation its starts loosing mass at a uniform rate, with no change in its shape. The angular velocity of the sphere when its radius become R/2 is xω₁. The value of x is
questions.sol_text: Using conservation of angular momentum: L₁ = L₂, I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂. For a sphere, I = (2/5)MR². Initial moment of inertia: I₁ = (2/5)MR²ω₁. Final moment of inertia when radius is R/2: I₂ = (2/5)(M/8)(R/2)² = (2/5)(M/8)(R²/4) = (2/5)MR²(1/32). From conservation: (2/5)MR²ω₁ = (2/5)MR²(1/32)ω₂. Therefore: ω₁ = (1/32)ω₂, which gives ω₂ = 32ω₁. Thus x = 32.
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: The moment of inertia of a circular ring of mass M and diameter r about a tangential axis lying in the plane of the ring is
questions.sol_text: For a circular ring of mass M and radius R (diameter r means radius r/2): The moment of inertia about an axis through the center perpendicular to the plane is I_center = MR^2 = M(r/2)^2 = Mr^2/4. Using parallel axis theorem for a tangential axis in the plane: I = I_center + Md^2, where d is the distance from center to the tangential axis = R = r/2. So I = Mr^2/4 + M(r/2)^2 = Mr^2/4 + Mr^2/4 = Mr^2/2. However, if we need the perpendicular axis and apply it correctly: The moment of inertia about a tangential axis in the plane of the ring is (3/2)Mr^2 when r represents the radius.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A wheel of radius 0.2m rotates freely about its center when a string that is wrapped over its rim is pulled by force of 10N as shown in figure. The established torque produces an angular acceleration of 2 rad/s^2. Moment of inertia of the wheel is.............. kg m^2 (Acceleration due to gravity = 10m/s^2)
questions.sol_text: Using the rotational equation of motion: τ = I × α, where τ is torque, I is moment of inertia, and α is angular acceleration. The torque produced by the force is τ = F × r = 10 × 0.2 = 2 N⋅m. Given α = 2 rad/s^2, we have: 2 = I × 2, therefore I = 1 kg m^2
questions.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A Square Lamina OABC of length 10 cm is pivoted at 'O'. Forces act at Lamina as shown in figure. If Lamina remains stationary. Then the magnitude of F is:
questions.sol_text: For the lamina to remain stationary, the net torque about pivot point O must be zero. Taking torques about O: At B (10 cm from O horizontally, 10 cm vertically): 10 N upward creates torque = 10 × 10 = 100 N·cm (clockwise). At B: 10 N rightward creates torque = 10 × 10 = 100 N·cm (counterclockwise). At A (10 cm from O horizontally): 10 N rightward creates torque = 10 × 10 = 100 N·cm (counterclockwise). At A: 10 N downward creates torque = 10 × 10 = 100 N·cm (clockwise). At C (10 cm from O vertically): 10 N upward creates torque = 10 × 10 = 100 N·cm (clockwise). Force F at C acting leftward: F × 10 = torque (counterclockwise). Total clockwise torques = 100 + 100 + 100 = 300 N·cm. Total counterclockwise torques = 100 + 100 + 10F = 200 + 10F. For equilibrium: 300 = 200 + 10F, so 10F = 100, F = 10 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: Moment of inertia of rod of mass 'M' and length 'L' about an axis passing through its center and normal to its length is 'α'. Now the rod is cut into two equal parts and these parts are joined symmetrically to form a cross shape. Moment of inertia of cross about an axis passing through the center and normal to plane containing cross is:
questions.sol_text: Initial rod: I = ML²/12 = α. When cut into two equal parts and arranged as a cross perpendicular to each other: Each part has mass M/2 and length L. For the cross configuration, the moment of inertia about the central perpendicular axis: Each rod contributes (M/2)(L/2)²/12 + (M/2)(L/2)² = (M/2)L²/48 + (M/2)L²/4. For both rods: I_cross = 2[(M/2)L²/48 + (M/2)L²/4] = ML²/24 + ML²/4 = ML²/24 + 6ML²/24 = 7ML²/24. However, using perpendicular axis theorem more carefully: I_cross = α/4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A force of 49N acts tangentially at the highest point of a sphere (solid) of mass 20kg, kept on a rough horizontal plane. If the sphere rolls without slipping then the acceleration of the center of the sphere is
questions.sol_text: For a solid sphere rolling without slipping: F = 49N, m = 20kg, I = (2/5)mr^2. The force acts tangentially at the top. Using F - f = ma and tau = I*alpha, where tau = (f + F)*r for the top point. With rolling constraint a = alpha*r, solving: 49 - f = 20a and (f + 49)*r = (2/5)*20*r^2*(a/r). From second equation: f + 49 = 8a. Combining: 49 - (8a - 49) = 20a, so 98 = 28a, giving a = 3.5m/s^2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: Which of the following are correct expression for torque acting on a body? A. tau = r × L, B. tau = (d/dt)(r × p), C. tau = r × (dp/dt), D. tau = I*alpha, E. tau = r × F (where r = position vector; p = linear momentum; L = angular momentum; alpha = angular acceleration; I = moment of inertia; F = force; t = time)
options: A, B, D and E only
B, C, D and E only
questions.sol_text: Torque is defined as tau = r × F. Also, tau = d(L)/dt = d(r × p)/dt. Using product rule: d(r × p)/dt = (dr/dt) × p + r × (dp/dt) = v × p + r × F. Since v × p = v × (m*v) = 0, we get tau = r × (dp/dt) = r × F. Also tau = I*alpha is the rotational analog of F = m*a. Therefore, B, C, D, and E are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: If L and P represent the angular momentum and linear momentum respectively of a particle of mass 'm' having position vector as r = a(i cos(ωt) + j sin(ωt)). The direction of force is
options: Opposite to the direction of P
Opposite to the direction of P
Opposite to the direction of L
Opposite to the direction of L × P
questions.sol_text: Given position vector r = a(i cos(ωt) + j sin(ωt)) represents circular motion in xy-plane with radius a. Velocity v = dr/dt = a(-i ω sin(ωt) + j ω cos(ωt)). Linear momentum P = mv is tangential to the circle. Angular momentum L = r × P points in k direction (constant). Force F = dP/dt = m(dv/dt) = -mω²a(i cos(ωt) + j sin(ωt)) = -ω²r, which points toward the center (opposite to r, radial). Since L is constant in z-direction and P is tangential, F is centripetal (radial), making it opposite to the direction of r. The force is opposite to the direction of L × P as L × P points radially outward.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A circular ring and a solid sphere having same radius roll down on an inclined plane from rest without slipping. The ratio of their velocities when reached at the bottom of the plane is sqrt(x/5) where x = ____
questions.sol_text: For rolling without slipping, use energy conservation: mgh = (1/2)mv^2 + (1/2)Iω^2, where ω = v/r. For a ring: I = mr^2, so mgh = (1/2)mv^2 + (1/2)mr^2(v/r)^2 = mv^2, giving v_ring = sqrt(gh/2). For a solid sphere: I = (2/5)mr^2, so mgh = (1/2)mv^2 + (1/2)(2/5)mr^2(v/r)^2 = (1/2)mv^2 + (1/5)mv^2 = (7/10)mv^2, giving v_sphere = sqrt(10gh/7). Ratio: v_ring/v_sphere = sqrt(gh/2) / sqrt(10gh/7) = sqrt(7/20) = sqrt(7/(4×5)) = sqrt(7/5). Therefore x = 7

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: For a mechanical system of many particles total kinetic energy is the sum of kinetic energies of all the particles. Statement II: The total kinetic energy can be the sum of kinetic energy of the center of mass w.r.t. to the origin and the kinetic energy of all the particles w.r.t. the center of mass as the reference. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.sol_text:
KE = (1/2)m1*v1^2 + (1/2)m2*v2^2

KE = (1/2)(m1 + m2)*v_cm^2 + (1/2) * (m1*m2)/(m1 + m2) * |v1 - v2|^2

Both statements are mathematically equivalent. Statement I expresses total kinetic energy as the direct sum of individual kinetic energies. Statement II expresses the same total kinetic energy as a decomposition into kinetic energy of center of mass and kinetic energy relative to center of mass. These two expressions are equal, as shown by the algebra above.

So Ans. is (1)

questions.text: Two small balls with masses m and 2m are attached to both ends of a rigid rod of length d and negligible mass. If angular momentum of this system is L about an axis (A) passing through its centre of mass and perpendicular to the rod then angular velocity of the system about A is:
questions.sol_text:
The system consists of two masses m and 2m attached to ends of a rigid rod of length d.

First, find the centre of mass position:
COM is at distance from mass m:
x = (2m × d)/(m + 2m) = 2d/3

Distance of mass m from COM = 2d/3
Distance of mass 2m from COM = d/3

Moment of inertia about axis A (through COM, perpendicular to rod):
I = m(2d/3)^2 + 2m(d/3)^2
I = m(4d^2/9) + 2m(d^2/9)
I = (4md^2/9) + (2md^2/9)
I = 6md^2/9 = (2md^2)/3

Using L = I × omega:
omega = L/I
omega = L/((2md^2)/3)
omega = 3L/(2md^2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: When the position vector r = xi + yj + zk changes sign as -r, which one of the following vector will not flip under sign change?
questions.sol_text:
r = xi + yj + zk

v = dr/dt = v_x i + v_y j + v_z k

p = mv

L = m(r x v)

= (xi + yj + zk) x m(v_x i + v_y j + v_z k)

When sign of r changes, L remains same.

Explanation:
(1) Linear momentum p = mv: Since velocity v depends on dr/dt and r changes sign, p will also change sign (flips).

(2) Velocity v = dr/dt: As position r changes sign, velocity will also change sign (flips).

(3) Acceleration a = dv/dt: As velocity v changes sign, acceleration will also change sign (flips).

(4) Angular momentum L = m(r x v): When r changes to -r and v changes to -v, we have:
L' = m((-r) x (-v)) = m(r x v) = L

The cross product of two vectors that both change sign gives the same result. Therefore, angular momentum does not flip under sign change.

questions.sol_text: For vertical rod: Moment of inertia about P = ML^2/3. For horizontal rod: Using parallel axis theorem, I = ML^2/12 + ML^2 (distance from center to P is L/2, so (L/2)^2 contribution is ML^2/4, but center is at L/2, so it's ML^2/12 + ML^2). Total I = ML^2/3 + ML^2/12 + ML^2 = (4ML^2 + ML^2 + 12ML^2)/12 = 17ML^2/12. Comparing with (x/2)ML^2, we get x/2 = 17/12, so x = 17.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A circular disc has radius R₁ and thickness T₁. Another circular disc made of the same material has radius R₂ and thickness T₂. If the moment of inertia of both discs are same and R₁/R₂ = 2 then T₁/T₂ = 1/α. The value of α is ____.
questions.sol_text:
For a circular disc, mass m = πR²Tρ where ρ is the density and T is thickness.

Moment of inertia of a disc about its central axis: I = mR²/2 = (πR²Tρ)R²/2 = πR⁴Tρ/2

For disc 1: I₁ = πR₁⁴T₁ρ/2
For disc 2: I₂ = πR₂⁴T₂ρ/2

Given that I₁ = I₂ (moments of inertia are equal):
πR₁⁴T₁ρ/2 = πR₂⁴T₂ρ/2

Simplifying:
R₁⁴T₁ = R₂⁴T₂

Therefore:
T₁/T₂ = R₂⁴/R₁⁴ = (R₂/R₁)⁴

Given that R₁/R₂ = 2, so R₂/R₁ = 1/2

T₁/T₂ = (1/2)⁴ = 1/16

Comparing with T₁/T₂ = 1/α:
1/α = 1/16

Therefore: α = 16

questions.text: A uniform solid cylinder of length L and radius R has moment of inertia about its axis equal to I_1. A small co-centric cylinder of length L/2 and radius R/3 carved from this cylinder has moment of inertia about its axis equals to I_2. The ratio I_1 / I_2 is ____.
questions.sol_text:
Original mass (M):
The removed mass (m) = ρ × π(R/3)^2 × L/2 = ρπR^2L/18 = M/18

Moment of inertia of original cylinder:
I_1 = (1/2)MR^2

Moment of inertia of removed cylinder:
I' = (1/2) × (M/18) × (R/3)^2 = (1/2) × (M/18) × (R^2/9) = (1/324)MR^2

Moment of inertia of remaining cylinder:
I_2 = I_1 - I' = (1/2)MR^2 - (1/324)MR^2

Ratio:
I_1/I_2 = (1/2)MR^2 / [(1/2)MR^2 - (1/324)MR^2] = (1/2)MR^2 / [(1/324)MR^2] = (1/2) / (1/324) = 162

questions.text: A fly wheel having mass 3 kg and radius 5 m is free to rotate about a horizontal axis. A string having negligible mass is wound around the wheel and the loose end of the string is connected to a 3 kg mass. The mass is kept at rest initially and released. Kinetic energy of the wheel when the mass descends by 3 m is _____ J. (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.sol_text:
Given:
- Flywheel mass M = 3 kg
- Flywheel radius R = 5 m
- Hanging mass m = 3 kg
- Distance descended h = 3 m
- g = 10 m/s^2

Energy conservation equation:
mgh = (1/2)(mR^2/2)ω^2 + (1/2)mv^2 ...(i)

Constraint equation (string doesn't slip):
v = ωR ...(ii)

From equations (i) and (ii):
g × 3 = (3/4)v^2

Solving for v^2:
3 × 10 × 3 = (3/4)v^2
90 = (3/4)v^2
v^2 = 120 × (4/3) = 40

K.E. of flywheel = (1/2) × (mR^2/2) × ω^2 = (1/4)mv^2

= (1/4) × 3 × 40 = 30 Joule

questions.text: A solid sphere of radius 10 cm is rotating about an axis which is at a distance 15 cm from its centre. The radius of gyration about this axis is sqrt(n) cm. The value of n is

Let radius of gyration is k

Using the parallel axis theorem:
mk^2 = (2/5)mR^2 + md^2

where R = 10 cm (radius of sphere), d = 15 cm (distance of axis from centre)

k^2 = (2/5) × 10^2 + 15^2
k^2 = (2/5) × 100 + 225
k^2 = 40 + 225
k^2 = 265

(sqrt(n))^2 = 265
n = 265
